author: pelican state news
title: Middle District of Louisiana announces juror qualification postcard mailing for June 15, 2026
text:
The Middle District of Louisiana announced on June 3 that it is in the process of qualifying jurors for future jury service. Residents who receive a Qualification Postcard in the mail are required by federal law to respond.
According to the announcement, receiving a questionnaire does not mean an individual has been summoned for jury duty or must appear at the courthouse. The court emphasized that the questionnaire is part of the qualification process only.
For those unable to respond online, if no response is received within ten days, a paper Qualification Questionnaire will be mailed automatically. The court advised recipients not to call to request a paper version.
Additional information about the juror qualification process can be found in the Jury FAQs provided by the Middle District. The court also warned that it will never ask for payment information or Social Security numbers as part of jury qualification or service at the Middle District of Louisiana.
The court encourages all recipients to complete their questionnaires promptly and remain vigilant against potential scams.
